nodes.name: Proof of the Evans-Spruck convergence lemma
nodes.statement:
The proof is exactly the same as that of \cite[Theorems 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3]{ES4}, with the difference that here we should substitute the domain of definition of all the functions (which is $\mathbb{R}^n$ in \cite{ES4}) with $\Omega_1\subset M$. This change leaves the proof unaltered, provided that the test functions used are taken to be in $C^\infty_c(\Omega_1\cup \partial\Omega)$, instead of $C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$. We also point out that hypothesis (3.2) used in \cite{ES4} should be replaced here with the convergence $ u_{\varepsilon_k}	o u$ in $C^0({\Omega_1}\cup\partial\Omega)$ and that of $
abla u_{\varepsilon_k}$ given in \eqref{Duetou}, and hypothesis (3.5) used in \cite{ES4} is still true in our case because of Lemma~ef{normalintest}, equation $(*_{\varepsilon_k})$ and the fact that $P$ is bounded. Finally, we remark that the result in \cite[Theorem 3.2]{ES4} is an intermediate step towards proving \cite[Theorem 3.3]{ES4} (which corresponds to (ii) here), which in our case is replaced by $\int_{\Omega_1} rac{
abla u_{\varepsilon_k}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k^2+|
abla u_{\varepsilon_k}|^2}}fd\mathcal{H}^n	o \int_{\Omega_1} rac {
abla u}{|
abla u|} fd\mathcal{H}^n$ for all $f\in L^1(\Omega_1;\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ with compact support in $(\Omega_1\cup\partial\Omega)\cap\{|
abla u|>0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat Evans-Spruck [ES4, Thms 3.1-3.3] on $\Omega_1\subset M$, with hypothesis (3.5) supplied by the integral estimate.

nodes.name: Transfer Evans-Spruck
nodes.statement: The proof is exactly the same as that of \cite[Theorems 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3]{ES4}, with the difference that here we should substitute the domain of definition of all the functions (which is $\mathbb{R}^n$ in \cite{ES4}) with $\Omega_1\subset M$. This change leaves the proof unaltered, provided that the test functions used are taken to be in $C^\infty_c(\Omega_1\cup \partial\Omega)$, instead of $C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat [ES4] with domain $\Omega_1\subset M$ and adapted test functions.

nodes.name: Verify hypotheses
nodes.statement: We also point out that hypothesis (3.2) used in \cite{ES4} should be replaced here with the convergence $ u_{\varepsilon_k}\to u$ in $C^0({\Omega_1}\cup\partial\Omega)$ and that of $\nabla u_{\varepsilon_k}$ given in \eqref{Duetou}, and hypothesis (3.5) used in \cite{ES4} is still true in our case because of Lemma~\ref{normalintest}, equation $(*_{\varepsilon_k})$ and the fact that $P$ is bounded.
nodes.statement_short: Hypotheses (3.2), (3.5) of [ES4] hold by the convergence and the integral estimate.

nodes.name: Intermediate step
nodes.statement_short: [ES4, Thm 3.2] is replaced by weak convergence of normalized gradients.

nodes.name: Gradient of weak solution vanishes on a null set
nodes.statement: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$, as in Definition~ \ref{weak}, then $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\{x\in \Omega_1||\nabla u|= 0)=0$.
assumptions: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$
nodes.label: nonfaten

nodes.name: Proof that $\{\nabla u=0\}$ is null
nodes.statement: The proof is exactly the same as that of \cite[Lemma 2.3]{MS}, replacing $\varepsilon_i$ and $\Omega$ with $\varepsilon_k$ and $\Omega_1\subset M$ respectively and the set $A$ with $A\cap W=\{x\in\Omega_1\cap W:Du(x)=0\}$ for any $W\subset\subset\Omega_1\cup\partial\Omega$. By the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.3]{MS}, we then obtain that $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(A\cap W)=0$ for any $W\subset\subset\Omega_1\cup\partial\Omega$ and thus the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Same as [MS, Lemma 2.3], localized to compact subsets $W$.

nodes.name: Strong $L^2_{loc}$ convergence of normalized gradients
nodes.label: ES conv2

nodes.name: Functions $U_\varepsilon$ and sets $\widetilde E^\varepsilon_t$, $\widetilde\Sigma^\varepsilon_t$
nodes.statement: For a solution $u_{\varepsilon}\in C^\infty(\Omega_0)$ of $(*_{\varepsilon})$ we define the function $U_{\varepsilon}:\Omega_0\times\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ by $U_{\varepsilon}(x,z)=u_{\varepsilon}(x)-\varepsilon z$ and we let \[\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon=\{(x,z)\in \Omega_0\times\mathbb{R}: U_{\varepsilon}(x,z)>t\}\] and \[\widetilde\Sigma^{\varepsilon}_t=\{(x,z)\in \Omega_0\times \mathbb{R}:U_{\varepsilon}(x,z)=t\}=\mathrm{graph}\left(\frac{u_{\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon}-\frac{t}{\varepsilon}\right),\] the latter being the hypersurfaces given by the level sets of $U_\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: $U_\varepsilon(x,z)=u_\varepsilon(x)-\varepsilon z$; its superlevel sets $\widetilde E^\varepsilon_t$ and level sets $\widetilde\Sigma^\varepsilon_t$ (translating graphs).
nodes.label: Ue

nodes.name: Mean curvature $H^\varepsilon_t$ and $P(u_\varepsilon)$
Mean curvature of $\widetilde\Sigma^\varepsilon_t$
nodes.statement: H^{\varepsilon}_t=\mathrm{div}\nu_\varepsilon=-P(u_{\varepsilon})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\nabla u_{\varepsilon}|^2+{\varepsilon}^2}},
nodes.label: MCet

nodes.name: Notation $P(\nu_\varepsilon)$
nodes.statement:
Note that $P(u_{\varepsilon})=\left(g^{ij}-
u^i_{\varepsilon}
u^j_{\varepsilon}ight) K_{ij}$, and thus we will also express this quantity as $P(
u_{\varepsilon})$.

nodes.name: $L^2$ bound on $H+P$ of translating graphs
nodes.statement: For any solution $u_{\varepsilon}\in C^\infty(\Omega_0)$ of $(*_{\varepsilon})$, any $t\in \mathbb{R}$ and any interval $I=[a,b]\subset \mathbb{R}$ the graph $\widetilde\Sigma^{\varepsilon}_t=\mathrm{graph}\left(\frac{u_{\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon}-\frac{t}{\varepsilon}\right)$ satisfies \[\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\widetilde\Sigma^{\varepsilon}_t\cap (\Omega_0\times I)}|H^\varepsilon_t+ P(\nu_\varepsilon)|^2d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}dt\le (b-a)\left(|\partial\Omega_0|+(n+2)\lambda|\Omega| \right), \] where $ \lambda=\max_i\{|\lambda_i|, \lambda_i\text{ eigenvalue of } K\}$ and the rest of the notation is as in Definition~\ref{Ue} and equation \eqref{MCet}.
nodes.label: H+Pk

nodes.name: Proof of the $L^2$ bound on $H+P$
nodes.statement:
Using the coarea formula and the expression of $H^\varepsilon_t$ given in \eqref{MCet}, we have \[ egin{split}\int_{\Omega_0	imes I} rac{1}{|\overline
abla U_{\varepsilon}|}dx&=\int_{\Omega_0	imes I} rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|^2} |\overline
abla U_{\varepsilon}|dx\ &=\int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\{(x,z):U_{\varepsilon}(x,z)=t\}\cap (\Omega_0	imes I)} rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|^2}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}dt\ &= \int_{0}^{\infty}\int_{\widetilde\Sigma^{\varepsilon}_t\cap (\Omega_0	imes I)}|H^{\varepsilon}_t+ P(
u_\varepsilon)|^2d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}dt, \end{split}\] where $\overline
abla=
abla^{M	imes\mathbb{R}}$. The result now follows by Lemma~ef{normalintest}.
nodes.statement_short: Coarea formula converts $\int 1/|\overline\nabla U_\varepsilon|$ into $\int\int|H+P|^2$, bounded by the integral estimate.

nodes.name: Outward minimization of area plus bulk energy for $\widetilde E^\varepsilon_t$
nodes.statement: For any solution $u_{\varepsilon}\in C^\infty(\Omega_0)$ of $(*_{\varepsilon})$ and any $t\in \mathbb{R}$ the set $\widetilde E^{\varepsilon}_t=\{U_\varepsilon>t\}$ satisfies the following minimization property. \[|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+\int_{W\cap \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^*F\cap W|+\int_{W\cap F} P(\nu_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\] for any compact set $W\subset \Omega\times\mathbb{R}$ and any finite perimeter set $F$ with $\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\subset F$ and $F\setminus \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\subset W$. Here, again we use the notation in Definition~\ref{Ue} and equation \eqref{MCet}.
nodes.statement_short: Superlevel sets $\{U_\varepsilon>t\}$ minimize area plus $\int P$ among outward perturbations.
nodes.label: emin

nodes.name: Calibration proof of outward minimization
nodes.statement:
Let $W$ and $F$ be as in the statement of the lemma and note that $F\setminus\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\subset\Omega_0	imes\mathbb{R}$. By $(*_{\hat \varepsilon})$ (see also \eqref{MCet}), we have that \[\mathrm{div} 
u_\varepsilon= -P(
u_\varepsilon)+ rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|}.\] The divergence theorem, using $
u_\varepsilon$ as a calibration, yields \[ egin{split}\int_{F\setminus \widetilde E^\varepsilon_t}-P(
u_\varepsilon)+ rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|}d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}=&-\int_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W}
u_\varepsilon\cdot 
u_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\ &+ \int_{\partial^* F\cap W}
u_\varepsilon\cdot 
u_{\partial^* F}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\ &\le-|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+|\partial^*F\cap W|, \end{split}\] where $
u_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon}$ and $
u_{\partial^* F}$ denote the outward pointing unit normals to $\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon$ and ${\partial^* F}$ respectively. Using this, along with the fact that $ rac{1}{|D U_{\varepsilon}|}>0$, we have \[ egin{split} |\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+\int_{W\cap \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}=&|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|-\int_{F\setminus \widetilde E^\varepsilon_t} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ &+\int_{W\cap F} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ \le& |\partial^*F\cap W| +\int_{W\cap F} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}. \end{split}\]
nodes.statement_short: Use the unit normal $\nu_\varepsilon$ as a calibration in the divergence theorem, with $1/|\overline\nabla U_\varepsilon|>0$.

nodes.name: Divergence of the normal
nodes.statement:
Let $W$ and $F$ be as in the statement of the lemma and note that $F\setminus\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\subset\Omega_0	imes\mathbb{R}$. By $(*_{\hat \varepsilon})$ (see also \eqref{MCet}), we have that \[\mathrm{div} 
u_\varepsilon= -P(
u_\varepsilon)+ rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|}.\]
nodes.statement_short:
By $(*_{\hat\varepsilon})$, $\mathrm{div}\,
u_\varepsilon=-P(
u_\varepsilon)+1/|\overline
abla U_\varepsilon|$.

nodes.name: Calibration inequality
nodes.statement:
The divergence theorem, using $
u_\varepsilon$ as a calibration, yields \[ egin{split}\int_{F\setminus \widetilde E^\varepsilon_t}-P(
u_\varepsilon)+ rac{1}{|\overline 
abla U_{\varepsilon}|}d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}=&-\int_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W}
u_\varepsilon\cdot 
u_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\ &+ \int_{\partial^* F\cap W}
u_\varepsilon\cdot 
u_{\partial^* F}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\ &\le-|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+|\partial^*F\cap W|, \end{split}\] where $
u_{\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon}$ and $
u_{\partial^* F}$ denote the outward pointing unit normals to $\partial^* \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon$ and ${\partial^* F}$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Divergence theorem with $\nu_\varepsilon$ as calibration.

nodes.name: Conclude minimization
nodes.statement:
Using this, along with the fact that $ rac{1}{|D U_{\varepsilon}|}>0$, we have \[ egin{split} |\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+\int_{W\cap \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}=&|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|-\int_{F\setminus \widetilde E^\varepsilon_t} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ &+\int_{W\cap F} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ \le& |\partial^*F\cap W| +\int_{W\cap F} P(
u_\varepsilon)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}. \end{split}\]
nodes.statement_short: Drop the positive term $1/|DU_\varepsilon|$ to get the minimizing inequality.

nodes.name: Local uniform area bound
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{emin} provides a local uniform area bound for $\partial^*\widetilde E^\varepsilon_t=\widetilde\Sigma^\varepsilon_t$ in $\Omega\times\mathbb{R}$ (since $K$, and thus $P$, is bounded).
nodes.label: area bound

nodes.name: Two-sided minimization for $\widetilde E^\varepsilon_t$
nodes.statement: Arguing similarly to the proof of Lemma~\ref{emin}, it is not hard to show that the sets $\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon$ actually minimize (not only on the outside) the following \[|\partial^*\widetilde E_t^\varepsilon\cap W|+\int_{W\cap \widetilde E_t^\varepsilon} P(\nu_\varepsilon)-\frac{1}{|\overline \nabla U_{\varepsilon}|}d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}.\] However, this will not be needed in this paper.
nodes.label: minimrmk

nodes.name: Limit function $U$ and sets $\widetilde E_t$, $\widetilde\Sigma_t$
nodes.statement:
Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$ and $\{u_{\varepsilon_k}\}\subset C^\infty(\Omega_0)$ be a sequence of solutions to the problems $(*_{\varepsilon_k})$ such that $ u_{\varepsilon_k}	o u$ in $C^0({\Omega_1}\cup\partial\Omega)$, as in Definition~ef{weak} (see also Theorem~ef{weak existence}). We define the function $U:\Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R}	o\mathbb{R}$ by \[U(x,z)=u(x).\] Note that $U\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R})$ and $U_{\varepsilon_k}	o U$ in $C^0(({\Omega_1}\cup\partial\Omega)	imes\mathbb{R})$, where the functions $U_{\varepsilon_k}$ are as in Definition~ef{Ue}. We, furthermore, set \[\widetilde E_t=\{(x,z)\in \Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R}: U(x,z)>t\}= E_t	imes\mathbb{R}\,,\,\,E_t=\{x\in \Omega_1:u(x)>t\}\] and \[\widetilde\Sigma_t=\partial \widetilde E_t=\Sigma_t	imes\mathbb{R}\,,\,\,\Sigma_t=\partial E_t.\] Finally, for notational simplicity, the sets $\widetilde E_t^{\varepsilon_k}$ and $\widetilde\Sigma_t^{\varepsilon_k}$, as defined in Definition~ef{Ue}, will be denoted by $\widetilde E_t^k$ and $\widetilde\Sigma_t^k$ respectively. Moreover, the upward pointing unit normal to $\widetilde\Sigma _t^k$ and its mean curvature will be denoted by $
u_k$ and $H_t^k$ respectively, so that equation \eqref{MCet} now reads  egin{equation} H_t^k=\mathrm{div}
u_k=-P(u_{\varepsilon_k})+ rac{1}{\sqrt{|
abla u_{\varepsilon_k}|^2+1}}, \end{equation} where recall that $P(u_{\varepsilon_k})=P(
u_k)=(g^{ij}-
u_k^i
u_k^j)K_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_short: $U(x,z)=u(x)$ with superlevel sets $\widetilde E_t=E_t\times\mathbb R$; notation $\widetilde E^k_t$, $\nu_k$, $H^k_t$ for the approximants.
nodes.label: U

nodes.name: Mean curvature of $\widetilde\Sigma^k_t$
nodes.statement: H_t^k=\mathrm{div}\nu_k=-P(u_{\varepsilon_k})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\nabla u_{\varepsilon_k}|^2+1}},
nodes.label: MCet2

nodes.name: Weak solutions are non-fattening
nodes.statement: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$. Then, for all $t>0$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\{u=t\})=0$.
assumptions: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$.
nodes.label: nonfat

nodes.name: Proof of non-fattening
nodes.statement:
The proof is exactly as that of \cite[Lemma 5.5]{S08}, where the same result is proven in the case $P=0$. We repeat the main step here and sketch the rest of the proof, using the notation of Definition~ef{U}. Let $0<t_1<t_2$ and $\Omega_1'=\Omega_1	imes I$ for some interval $I=(a,b)$. By using the coarea formula, \eqref{MCet2}, H"older's inequality, Remark~ef{area bound}, and Lemma~ef{H+Pk}, we obtain \[ egin{split} |\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_1}^k\cap\Omega_1')-\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_2}^k\cap\Omega_1')|&=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_{\widetilde\Sigma^k_t\cap\Omega_1'}|H_t^k+P(
u_k)|\ &\le C|t_2-t_1|^ rac12, \end{split}\] where $C$ is a constant independent on $k$. Let now $S=\{t>0:\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\{U=t\}>0\}=\{t>0:\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\{u=t\}>0\}$ and note that for any $t
otin S$ $\widetilde E_t^k	o\widetilde E_t$ in $L^1_	ext{loc}$ (in the sense that their characteristic functions converge in $L^1_	ext{loc}(\Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R})$), because of the local uniform convergence $U_{\varepsilon_k}	o U$ in $\Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R}$. Thus, for $t_1,t_2
otin S$, the limit of the above estimate yields \[|\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_1}\cap\Omega_1')-\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_2}\cap\Omega_1')|\le C|t_2-t_1|^ rac12.\] For any $t\in S$ (a countable set) we can now pick two sequences of times $t_1^j<t<t_2^j$ for which the above is true and such that both sequences tend to $t$. This then implies that $\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\{U=t\}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Following [S08, Lemma 5.5]: the volume of $\widetilde E^k_t$ is H\"older-1/2 in $t$ uniformly in $k$, which passes to the limit and rules out fat level sets.

nodes.name: Follow Schulze
nodes.statement: The proof is exactly as that of \cite[Lemma 5.5]{S08}, where the same result is proven in the case $P=0$. We repeat the main step here and sketch the rest of the proof, using the notation of Definition~\ref{U}.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt [S08, Lemma 5.5] (case $P=0$).

nodes.name: H\"older continuity in $t$
nodes.statement: Let $0<t_1<t_2$ and $\Omega_1'=\Omega_1\times I$ for some interval $I=(a,b)$. By using the coarea formula, \eqref{MCet2}, H\"older's inequality, Remark~\ref{area bound}, and Lemma~\ref{H+Pk}, we obtain \[\begin{split} |\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_1}^k\cap\Omega_1')-\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_2}^k\cap\Omega_1')|&=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_{\widetilde\Sigma^k_t\cap\Omega_1'}|H_t^k+P(\nu_k)|\\ &\le C|t_2-t_1|^\frac12, \end{split}\] where $C$ is a constant independent on $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Coarea, H\"older and the $L^2$ bound give $|\Delta\mathrm{vol}|\le C|t_2-t_1|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Let now $S=\{t>0:\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\{U=t\}>0\}=\{t>0:\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\{u=t\}>0\}$ and note that for any $t\notin S$ $\widetilde E_t^k\to\widetilde E_t$ in $L^1_\text{loc}$ (in the sense that their characteristic functions converge in $L^1_\text{loc}(\Omega_1\times\mathbb{R})$), because of the local uniform convergence $U_{\varepsilon_k}\to U$ in $\Omega_1\times\mathbb{R}$. Thus, for $t_1,t_2\notin S$, the limit of the above estimate yields \[|\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_1}\cap\Omega_1')-\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(\widetilde E_{t_2}\cap\Omega_1')|\le C|t_2-t_1|^\frac12.\]
nodes.statement_short: For $t_1,t_2\notin S$ the estimate passes to the limit.

nodes.name: Approximate from both sides
nodes.statement: For any $t\in S$ (a countable set) we can now pick two sequences of times $t_1^j<t<t_2^j$ for which the above is true and such that both sequences tend to $t$. This then implies that $\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\{U=t\}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $t\in S$ from both sides to get a null level set.

nodes.name: $L^1_{loc}$ convergence of superlevel sets
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{nonfat}, along with the uniform convergence $U_{\varepsilon_k}\to U$, implies that $\widetilde E_t^k\to \widetilde E_t$ in $L^1_\text{loc}(\Omega_1\times\mathbb{R})$ (i.e. the corresponding characteristic functions converge in $L^1_\text{loc}(\Omega_1\times\mathbb{R})$, see also proof of \cite[Lemma 5.5]{S08}).
nodes.label: setconv

nodes.name: Outward minimization passes to the weak solution
nodes.statement:
For any weak solution $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ of $(**)$ and any $t\in \mathbb{R}$ the set $\widetilde E_t=\{U>t\}$ satisfies the following minimization property. \[|\partial^*\widetilde E_t\cap W|+\int_{W\cap \widetilde E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^*F\cap W|+\int_{W\cap F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\] for any compact set $W\subset \Omega	imes\mathbb{R}$ and any finite perimeter set $F$ with $\widetilde E_t\subset F$ and $F\setminus \widetilde E_t\subset W$. Here, $P(
u)=\left(g^{ij}-
u^i
u^jight) K_{ij}$ and $
u$ is independent of the vertical component with $
u(x,z)= 
u(x)= rac{Du}{|Du|}(x)$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\Omega_1$, and we use the notation in Definition~ef{U}.. Furthermore, the same minimizing property is satisfied by $E_t$ in $\Omega_1$, that is \[ egin{split} |\partial^* E_t\cap W|+\int_{ W\cap E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\le |\partial^* F\cap W|+ \int_{W\cap F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1} \end{split}\] for any compact set $W\subset\Omega$ and any finite perimeter set $F$ with $ E_t\subset F$ and $F\setminus E_t\subset W$.
nodes.statement_short: The sets $\{U>t\}$ and $E_t=\{u>t\}$ minimize area plus $\int P$ among outward perturbations.
nodes.label: eminu

nodes.name: Proof that outward minimization passes to the limit
nodes.statement:
The proof follows that of \cite[Lemma 5.6, Corollary 5.7]{S08}, where the same statements are proven in the case when $P=0$. Let $W$, $F$ be as in the statement of the lemma and note that $F\setminus\widetilde E_t\subset\Omega_1	imes\mathbb{R}$. First, note that arguing exactly as in \cite[Lemma 5.6]{S08}, we can assume, by passing to a slightly larger compact set if necessary, that for $W$ the following is true. The boundary $\partial W$ is smooth, $|\partial^*(F\cup \widetilde E_t^k)\cap\partial W|=|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap\partial W|=|\partial^* \widetilde E_t^k\cap\partial W|=0$ for all $k$ and $\lim_{k	o\infty}\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}= 0$, where $\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}$ and $\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}$ are the inner and outer trace of ${F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}$ and $\widetilde E_t^k$ on $\partial W$ (see \cite[Chapter 2]{Giu} and \cite[Section 2.4]{Alex} for definitions of the traces and note that here we also use Remark~ef{setconv}). Let now $F^k= \widetilde E_t^k\cup (F\cap W)$. We then have \[ egin{split}|\partial^*F^k\cap W|=&\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}+|\partial^*(F\cup \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|\ =&\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}+ |\partial^* \widetilde E^k_t\cap W|\ &+ |\partial^* F\cap W|-|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|, \end{split}\] where the second equality above is justified by arguing as in \cite[(36) of proof Lemma~5.6]{S08}). By the minimizing property of $\widetilde E_t^k$ (since $F^k\supset \widetilde E_t^k$), we have \[|\partial^* \widetilde E^k_t\cap W|-\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^* F^k\cap W|,\] and thus we obtain \[ egin{split} |\partial^* F\cap W|\ge &|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|- \int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ &-\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}. \end{split}\] Since the last term on the right-hand side vanishes as $k	o \infty$ and $|\partial^* \widetilde E_t\cap W|=|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t)\cap W| \le \lim_{k	o\infty}|\partial^*(F\cap\widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|$ (by Remark~ef{setconv} and the lower semi-continuity, see \cite[Theorem 1.9]{Giu} and \cite[Theorem 2.38]{Alex}), it suffices to show that \[\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2} \stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}, \] where $
u$ is as in the statement of the lemma. To see this, we note that $W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)=(F\cap W)\setminus\widetilde E_t^k$ and $ W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)=(F\cap W)\setminus \widetilde E_t$, and we write \[ egin{split}\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} &P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}-\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2} \ =& \int_{W\cap F\cap(\widetilde E_t\setminus\widetilde E_t^k)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}-\int_{W\cap F\cap(\widetilde E^k_t\setminus\widetilde E_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ &+ \int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u_k)-P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}. \end{split}\] We can see now that the right-hand side of the above equality tends to $0$, as $k	o \infty$, because of the fact that $P$ is bounded, Remark~ef{setconv} and Lemma~ef{ES conv}. More specifically, we have the following two observations. First, by Remark~ef{setconv}, we have \[\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(W\cap (\widetilde E_t\setminus \widetilde E^k_t))\,,\,\, \mathcal{H}^{n+2}(W\cap (\widetilde E_t^k\setminus \widetilde E_t))\stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0,\] which implies that the first two terms tend to zero. Second, by Lemma~ef{ES conv} (see also Remark~ef{ES conv2}), we have \[\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} 
u_k^i-
u^id\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le C(W)\|
u_k-
u\|_{L^2(W)} \stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}0,\] and thus, by writing $
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^j=
u_k^i(
u_k^j-
u^j)+
u^j(
u_k^i-
u^i)$, we have \[\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} 
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^jd\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}0.\] Since $P(
u_k)- P(
u)= (
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^j) K_{ij}$, this implies that the last term also tends to zero. Finally, one can easily see that the same minimization property holds for $E_t$ in $\Omega_1$ as follows (cf. \cite[Corollary 5.7]{S08}). Let $W\subset \Omega$ be a compact set and let $F$ be a finite perimeter set such that $E_t\subset F$ and $F\setminus E_t\subset W$. Given any $\ell>0$, let $\widetilde F=(F	imes(-\ell,\ell))\cup \widetilde E_t$. Using the minimization property of $\widetilde E_t$, we have \[|\partial^*\widetilde E_t\cap \widetilde W|+\int_{\widetilde W\cap \widetilde E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^*\widetilde F\cap \widetilde W|+\int_{\widetilde W\cap \widetilde F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2},\] where $\widetilde W=W	imes[-2\ell, 2\ell]$. This then yields \[ egin{split} 2\ell|\partial^* E_t\cap W|+2\ell \int_{ W\cap E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\le& 2\ell|\partial^* F\cap W|+2\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(F\setminus E_t)\ &+2\ell \int_{W\cap F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}. \end{split}\] Dividing by $\ell$ and letting $\ell	o \infty$ provides the required property.
nodes.statement_short: Following [S08, Lemma 5.6], compare with $F^k=\widetilde E^k_t\cup(F\cap W)$ and pass to the limit using lower semicontinuity and strong convergence of normals for the $P$-term. Then slab competitors give the property for $E_t$.

nodes.name: Follow Schulze
nodes.statement: The proof follows that of \cite[Lemma 5.6, Corollary 5.7]{S08}, where the same statements are proven in the case when $P=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt [S08, Lemma 5.6, Cor. 5.7].

nodes.name: Choice of $W$
nodes.statement: Let $W$, $F$ be as in the statement of the lemma and note that $F\setminus\widetilde E_t\subset\Omega_1\times\mathbb{R}$. First, note that arguing exactly as in \cite[Lemma 5.6]{S08}, we can assume, by passing to a slightly larger compact set if necessary, that for $W$ the following is true. The boundary $\partial W$ is smooth, $|\partial^*(F\cup \widetilde E_t^k)\cap\partial W|=|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap\partial W|=|\partial^* \widetilde E_t^k\cap\partial W|=0$ for all $k$ and $\lim_{k\to\infty}\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}= 0$, where $\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}$ and $\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}$ are the inner and outer trace of ${F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}$ and $\widetilde E_t^k$ on $\partial W$ (see \cite[Chapter 2]{Giu} and \cite[Section 2.4]{Alex} for definitions of the traces and note that here we also use Remark~\ref{setconv}).
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge $W$ so its boundary is smooth and traces behave.

nodes.name: Competitors $F^k$
nodes.statement: Let now $F^k= \widetilde E_t^k\cup (F\cap W)$. We then have \[\begin{split}|\partial^*F^k\cap W|=&\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}+|\partial^*(F\cup \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|\\ =&\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}+ |\partial^* \widetilde E^k_t\cap W|\\ &+ |\partial^* F\cap W|-|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|, \end{split}\] where the second equality above is justified by arguing as in \cite[(36) of proof Lemma~5.6]{S08}).
nodes.statement_short: Define $F^k=\widetilde E^k_t\cup(F\cap W)$ and compute its perimeter.

nodes.name: Apply minimization of $\widetilde E^k_t$
nodes.statement: By the minimizing property of $\widetilde E_t^k$ (since $F^k\supset \widetilde E_t^k$), we have \[|\partial^* \widetilde E^k_t\cap W|-\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^* F^k\cap W|,\] and thus we obtain \[\begin{split} |\partial^* F\cap W|\ge &|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|- \int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\\ &-\int_{\partial W} |\phi^-_{F\cup \widetilde E_t^k}-\phi^+_{\widetilde E_t^k}|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}. \end{split}\]
nodes.statement_short: Use the outward minimization of $\widetilde E^k_t$.

nodes.name: Reduction to $P$-term convergence
nodes.statement:
Since the last term on the right-hand side vanishes as $k	o \infty$ and $|\partial^* \widetilde E_t\cap W|=|\partial^*(F\cap \widetilde E_t)\cap W| \le \lim_{k	o\infty}|\partial^*(F\cap\widetilde E_t^k)\cap W|$ (by Remark~ef{setconv} and the lower semi-continuity, see \cite[Theorem 1.9]{Giu} and \cite[Theorem 2.38]{Alex}), it suffices to show that \[\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2} \stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}, \] where $
u$ is as in the statement of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: By lower semicontinuity it suffices to show convergence of the $P$-integrals.

nodes.name: Split the difference
nodes.statement:
To see this, we note that $W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)=(F\cap W)\setminus\widetilde E_t^k$ and $ W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)=(F\cap W)\setminus \widetilde E_t$, and we write \[ egin{split}\int_{W\cap (F^k\setminus \widetilde E^k_t)} &P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}-\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2} \ =& \int_{W\cap F\cap(\widetilde E_t\setminus\widetilde E_t^k)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}-\int_{W\cap F\cap(\widetilde E^k_t\setminus\widetilde E_t)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\ &+ \int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} P(
u_k)-P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}. \end{split}\]
nodes.statement_short: Split the difference of $P$-integrals into three terms.

nodes.name: Each term vanishes
nodes.statement:
We can see now that the right-hand side of the above equality tends to $0$, as $k	o \infty$, because of the fact that $P$ is bounded, Remark~ef{setconv} and Lemma~ef{ES conv}. More specifically, we have the following two observations. First, by Remark~ef{setconv}, we have \[\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(W\cap (\widetilde E_t\setminus \widetilde E^k_t))\,,\,\, \mathcal{H}^{n+2}(W\cap (\widetilde E_t^k\setminus \widetilde E_t))\stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0,\] which implies that the first two terms tend to zero. Second, by Lemma~ef{ES conv} (see also Remark~ef{ES conv2}), we have \[\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} 
u_k^i-
u^id\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le C(W)\|
u_k-
u\|_{L^2(W)} \stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}0,\] and thus, by writing $
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^j=
u_k^i(
u_k^j-
u^j)+
u^j(
u_k^i-
u^i)$, we have \[\int_{W\cap (F\setminus \widetilde E_t)} 
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^jd\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\stackrel{k	o \infty}{\longrightarrow}0.\] Since $P(
u_k)- P(
u)= (
u_k^i
u_k^j-
u^i
u^j) K_{ij}$, this implies that the last term also tends to zero.
nodes.statement_short: Set convergence and $L^2$ convergence of normals make each term vanish.

nodes.name: Property for $E_t$
nodes.statement:
Finally, one can easily see that the same minimization property holds for $E_t$ in $\Omega_1$ as follows (cf. \cite[Corollary 5.7]{S08}). Let $W\subset \Omega$ be a compact set and let $F$ be a finite perimeter set such that $E_t\subset F$ and $F\setminus E_t\subset W$. Given any $\ell>0$, let $\widetilde F=(F	imes(-\ell,\ell))\cup \widetilde E_t$. Using the minimization property of $\widetilde E_t$, we have \[|\partial^*\widetilde E_t\cap \widetilde W|+\int_{\widetilde W\cap \widetilde E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le |\partial^*\widetilde F\cap \widetilde W|+\int_{\widetilde W\cap \widetilde F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2},\] where $\widetilde W=W	imes[-2\ell, 2\ell]$. This then yields \[ egin{split} 2\ell|\partial^* E_t\cap W|+2\ell \int_{ W\cap E_t} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\le& 2\ell|\partial^* F\cap W|+2\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(F\setminus E_t)\ &+2\ell \int_{W\cap F} P(
u)d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}. \end{split}\] Dividing by $\ell$ and letting $\ell	o \infty$ provides the required property.
nodes.statement_short: Use slab competitors $F\times(-\ell,\ell)$ and let $\ell\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Measures $\mu^k_t$ and $\mu_t$
nodes.statement: We now define the measures \begin{equation*} \mu_t^k=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \widetilde \Sigma_t^k \text{ and }\mu_t=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^*\widetilde E_t, \end{equation*} where recall that $\widetilde \Sigma_t^k=\partial(\{(x, z): U_{\varepsilon_k}(x,z)>t\})=\mathrm{graph} \left(\frac{u_{\varepsilon_k}}{\varepsilon_k}-\frac{t}{\varepsilon_k}\right)$ (see Definition~\ref{U}).

nodes.name: Level sets agree with reduced boundaries a.e.
nodes.statement: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$. Then, for a.e. $t\in[0,\infty)$, $\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\}\setminus\partial^*\{u>t\})=0$
assumptions: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$.
nodes.label: bdrystar

nodes.name: Proof via the coarea formulas
nodes.statement: This is proven exactly as \cite[Lemma 5.9]{S08}. Since $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega)\subset \text{BV}(\Omega)$ we can compare the coarea formula for BV-functions and Lipschitz functions to obtain \[\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\partial^*E_t)dt=\int_{\Omega_1\cap\{u<T\}}|\nabla u|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}=\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\})dt\] for any $T>0$, and thus \[\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\}\setminus\partial^* E_t)dt=0,\] which yields that $\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\}\setminus\partial^* E_t)=0$ for a.e. $t\in [0,T]$. Since this is true for all $T>0$, we obtain the result.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the BV and Lipschitz coarea formulas, as in [S08, Lemma 5.9].

nodes.name: Follow Schulze
nodes.statement: This is proven exactly as \cite[Lemma 5.9]{S08}.
nodes.statement_short: As in [S08, Lemma 5.9].

nodes.name: Compare coarea formulas
nodes.statement: Since $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega)\subset \text{BV}(\Omega)$ we can compare the coarea formula for BV-functions and Lipschitz functions to obtain \[\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\partial^*E_t)dt=\int_{\Omega_1\cap\{u<T\}}|\nabla u|d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}=\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\})dt\] for any $T>0$, and thus \[\int_0^T\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\}\setminus\partial^* E_t)dt=0,\] which yields that $\mathcal{H}^n(\{u=t\}\setminus\partial^* E_t)=0$ for a.e. $t\in [0,T]$.
nodes.statement_short: Equate the BV and Lipschitz coarea formulas.

nodes.name: All $T$
nodes.statement: Since this is true for all $T>0$, we obtain the result.
nodes.statement_short: Let $T\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Convergence of $\mu^k_t$ to $\mu_t$ as Radon measures
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_t^k=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \widetilde \Sigma_t^k$ and $\mu_t=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^*\widetilde E_t$ (where we use the notation of Definition~\ref{U}). Then, for a.e $t>0$ $\mu_t^k\stackrel{k\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}\mu_t$ as Radon measures.
nodes.label: mainconvergence

nodes.name: Proof of the measure convergence
nodes.statement:
The proof is almost identical to that of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08}. We go through the proof here pointing out the differences in our case. To fit our notation, one has to replace $i$, $\varepsilon_i$, $\Omega$, $E_t^i$, $N_t^i$, $E'_t$ and $\Gamma_t$ of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} by $k$, $\varepsilon_k$, $\Omega_0$, $\widetilde E_t^k$, $\widetilde E_t$, $\widetilde \Sigma_t^k$ and $\Sigma_t$ respectively. Note first that, by Lemma~ef{bdrystar}, for almost every $t$ $\mu_t= \mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \widetilde \Sigma_t$, where recall that $\widetilde \Sigma_t=\partial \widetilde E_t=\Sigma_t	imes\mathbb{R}=\partial E_t	imes\mathbb{R}$. Fix a $t>0$, so that the above is true. By the minimizing property (Lemma~ef{emin}, Remark~ef{area bound}), $|\widetilde \Sigma^k_t|$ are locally uniformly bounded and thus, after passing to a subsequence, $\mu_t^k\stackrel{k	o\infty}{\longrightarrow}\mu$, where $\mu$ is a Radon measure in $\Omega_0	imes\mathbb{R}$ (note that here we keep the same notation for the subsequence, whereas in \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} the subsequence is denoted by $\{\mu_t^{i_j}\}_j\subset\{\mu_t^i\}_i$, so to fit our notation one has to further replace $i_j$ of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} by $k$).\ { f Claim 1:} $\mathrm{spt} \mu\subset\{u=t\}	imes\mathbb{R}$.\ The proof of Claim 1 is identical to that of \cite[Claim 1 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}.\ { f Claim 2:} For $B_ho(x)\subset\subset\Omega_0	imes\mathbb{R}$ \[\mu(\overline B_ho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial B_ho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(B_ho(x)).\] The proof of Claim 2 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, with the only difference being the bound for $\mu^{k}_t(B_ho(x))=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial^* \widetilde E_t^k\cap B_ho(x))$. In particular, here using Lemma~ef{emin} with $F= \widetilde E_t^k\cup B_ho(x)$, we obtain \[\mu^{k}_t(B_ho(x))+\int_{\widetilde E_t^k\cap B_ho(x)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_ho(x))+\int_{ B_ho(x)} P(
u_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2},\] which yields \[ \mu^{k}_t(B_ho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_ho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}( B_ho(x)).\] We have then, as in \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure (since the $\mathcal{H}^{n+2}$-measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure). Thus, by the Radon-Nikodym theorem, Claim 1, and Lemma~ef{bdrystar}, we obtain that there exists a function $	heta\in L^\infty(\Sigma_t	imes\mathbb{R}, \mathcal{H}^{n+1})$ such that  egin{equation} \mu=(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(\partial^*E_t	imes\mathbb{R}))\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu	heta=\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu	heta, \end{equation} where recall that $\Sigma_t=\partial E_t$. 
oindent{ f Claim 3:} $	heta\ge 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\Sigma_t	imes\mathbb{R}$.\ The proof of Claim 3 is identical to that of \cite[Claim 3 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}.\ { f Claim 4:} $	heta\le 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\partial^*E_t$.\ The proof of Claim 4 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 4 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08} with the only difference being the way we obtain the bound for $\mu_\lambda^{k}(B_1)= \lambda^{-(n+2)}\mu_t^{k}(\lambda B_1)$ (denoted as $\mu_\lambda^{i_j}$ in \cite[line 20, page 221]{S08}). In particular, here, one has to use the minimizing property of $E_t^k$ given in Lemma~ef{emin} (whereas in \cite{S08} $E_t^k$ are minimizing area on the outside). This, however, does not change the argument as it only changes the bound by a term of order $\varepsilon$. More specifically, the term $\sup_{S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1}|P(
u_k)||S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1|$ should be added to the bound. Here, $P(
u_\kappa)$ is the term appearing in Lemma~ef{emin} and $S_{2\varepsilon}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^{n+2}:|x_{n+2}|\le 2\varepsilon\}$ as in \cite{S08}. We remark also that in the proof of this claim, one uses ``rescalings'' of sets in $M	imes\mathbb{R}$ and of the measures $\mu_t^k, \mu_t$, which are defined via the exponential map. In particular one makes the identifications \[(B_ho(x), g)\simeq(B_ho(\vec 0), \exp^*_x g)\simeq (B_ho(0), \hat g_{ij}^\phi)\] as Riemannian manifolds, where $(B_ho(x), \phi)$ are the geodesic normal coordinates that correspond to the identification $(T_pM, g(p))\simeq(R^{n+2}, \langle\cdot,\cdotangle)$ as Hilbert spaces and $\hat g_{ij}^\phi=g_{ij}^\phi\circ\phi^{-1}$, where $\hat g_{ij}^\phi$ are the components of $g$ in geodesic normal coordinates. These identifications allow us to reduce the proof to the case that $M=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. nodes.name: Setup and subsequential limit
nodes.statement: The proof is almost identical to that of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08}. We go through the proof here pointing out the differences in our case. To fit our notation, one has to replace $i$, $\varepsilon_i$, $\Omega$, $E_t^i$, $N_t^i$, $E'_t$ and $\Gamma_t$ of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} by $k$, $\varepsilon_k$, $\Omega_0$, $\widetilde E_t^k$, $\widetilde E_t$, $\widetilde \Sigma_t^k$ and $\Sigma_t$ respectively. Note first that, by Lemma~\ref{bdrystar}, for almost every $t$ $\mu_t= \mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \widetilde \Sigma_t$, where recall that $\widetilde \Sigma_t=\partial \widetilde E_t=\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}=\partial E_t\times\mathbb{R}$. Fix a $t>0$, so that the above is true. By the minimizing property (Lemma~\ref{emin}, Remark~\ref{area bound}), $|\widetilde \Sigma^k_t|$ are locally uniformly bounded and thus, after passing to a subsequence, $\mu_t^k\stackrel{k\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}\mu$, where $\mu$ is a Radon measure in $\Omega_0\times\mathbb{R}$ (note that here we keep the same notation for the subsequence, whereas in \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} the subsequence is denoted by $\{\mu_t^{i_j}\}_j\subset\{\mu_t^i\}_i$, so to fit our notation one has to further replace $i_j$ of \cite[Proposition 5.10]{S08} by $k$).
nodes.statement_short: Translate [S08, Prop. 5.10] notation and extract a limit measure $\mu$ from area bounds.

nodes.name: Claim 1
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 1:} $\mathrm{spt} \mu\subset\{u=t\}\times\mathbb{R}$.\\ The proof of Claim 1 is identical to that of \cite[Claim 1 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}.
nodes.statement_short: Support of $\mu$ lies in $\{u=t\}\times\mathbb R$, as in [S08].

nodes.name: Claim 2
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 2:} For $B_\rho(x)\subset\subset\Omega_0\times\mathbb{R}$ \[\mu(\overline B_\rho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial B_\rho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(B_\rho(x)).\] The proof of Claim 2 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, with the only difference being the bound for $\mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial^* \widetilde E_t^k\cap B_\rho(x))$. In particular, here using Lemma~\ref{emin} with $F= \widetilde E_t^k\cup B_\rho(x)$, we obtain \[\mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))+\int_{\widetilde E_t^k\cap B_\rho(x)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_\rho(x))+\int_{ B_\rho(x)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2},\] which yields \[ \mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_\rho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}( B_\rho(x)).\] We have then, as in \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure (since the $\mathcal{H}^{n+2}$-measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure). Thus, by the Radon-Nikodym theorem, Claim 1, and Lemma~\ref{bdrystar}, we obtain that there exists a function $\theta\in L^\infty(\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}, \mathcal{H}^{n+1})$ such that \begin{equation} \mu=(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(\partial^*E_t\times\mathbb{R}))\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta=\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta, \end{equation} where recall that $\Sigma_t=\partial E_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Density upper bound for $\mu$ on balls, hence $\mu=\mu_t\llcorner\theta$.

nodes.name: Ball competitor
nodes.statement: The proof of Claim 2 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, with the only difference being the bound for $\mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial^* \widetilde E_t^k\cap B_\rho(x))$. In particular, here using Lemma~\ref{emin} with $F= \widetilde E_t^k\cup B_\rho(x)$, we obtain \[\mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))+\int_{\widetilde E_t^k\cap B_\rho(x)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2}\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_\rho(x))+\int_{ B_\rho(x)} P(\nu_k)d\mathcal{H}^{n+2},\] which yields \[ \mu^{k}_t(B_\rho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}( \partial B_\rho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}( B_\rho(x)).\]
nodes.statement_short: Use outward minimization with $F=\widetilde E^k_t\cup B_\rho(x)$.

nodes.name: Radon-Nikodym density
nodes.statement: We have then, as in \cite[Claim 2 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}, that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure (since the $\mathcal{H}^{n+2}$-measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-measure). Thus, by the Radon-Nikodym theorem, Claim 1, and Lemma~\ref{bdrystar}, we obtain that there exists a function $\theta\in L^\infty(\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}, \mathcal{H}^{n+1})$ such that \begin{equation} \mu=(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(\partial^*E_t\times\mathbb{R}))\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta=\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta, \end{equation} where recall that $\Sigma_t=\partial E_t$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu$ is absolutely continuous, so $\mu=\mu_t\llcorner\theta$.

nodes.name: Claim 3
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 3:} $\theta\ge 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}$.\\ The proof of Claim 3 is identical to that of \cite[Claim 3 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08}.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta\ge1$, as in [S08].

nodes.name: Claim 4
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 4:} $\theta\le 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\partial^*E_t$.\\ The proof of Claim 4 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 4 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08} with the only difference being the way we obtain the bound for $\mu_\lambda^{k}(B_1)= \lambda^{-(n+2)}\mu_t^{k}(\lambda B_1)$ (denoted as $\mu_\lambda^{i_j}$ in \cite[line 20, page 221]{S08}). In particular, here, one has to use the minimizing property of $E_t^k$ given in Lemma~\ref{emin} (whereas in \cite{S08} $E_t^k$ are minimizing area on the outside). This, however, does not change the argument as it only changes the bound by a term of order $\varepsilon$. More specifically, the term $\sup_{S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1}|P(\nu_k)||S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1|$ should be added to the bound. Here, $P(\nu_\kappa)$ is the term appearing in Lemma~\ref{emin} and $S_{2\varepsilon}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^{n+2}:|x_{n+2}|\le 2\varepsilon\}$ as in \cite{S08}. We remark also that in the proof of this claim, one uses ``rescalings'' of sets in $M\times\mathbb{R}$ and of the measures $\mu_t^k, \mu_t$, which are defined via the exponential map. In particular one makes the identifications \[(B_\rho(x), g)\simeq(B_\rho(\vec 0), \exp^*_x g)\simeq (B_\rho(0), \hat g_{ij}^\phi)\] as Riemannian manifolds, where $(B_\rho(x), \phi)$ are the geodesic normal coordinates that correspond to the identification $(T_pM, g(p))\simeq(R^{n+2}, \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ as Hilbert spaces and $\hat g_{ij}^\phi=g_{ij}^\phi\circ\phi^{-1}$, where $\hat g_{ij}^\phi$ are the components of $g$ in geodesic normal coordinates. These identifications allow us to reduce the proof to the case that $M=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. We remark also that, since $\exp^{-1}$ is an isometry, the minimizing property given in Lemma~\ref{emin} and Claim 2 (both of which are used in the proof of this claim) are preserved under these identifications. For a detailed discussion and proofs of these facts see \cite{Alex}.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta\le1$ on $\partial^*E_t$, adapting [S08] with an $O(\varepsilon)$ $P$-correction.

nodes.name: Modified bound
nodes.statement: The proof of Claim 4 is the same as that of \cite[Claim 4 of proof of Proposition 5.10]{S08} with the only difference being the way we obtain the bound for $\mu_\lambda^{k}(B_1)= \lambda^{-(n+2)}\mu_t^{k}(\lambda B_1)$ (denoted as $\mu_\lambda^{i_j}$ in \cite[line 20, page 221]{S08}). In particular, here, one has to use the minimizing property of $E_t^k$ given in Lemma~\ref{emin} (whereas in \cite{S08} $E_t^k$ are minimizing area on the outside). This, however, does not change the argument as it only changes the bound by a term of order $\varepsilon$. More specifically, the term $\sup_{S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1}|P(\nu_k)||S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1|$ should be added to the bound. Here, $P(\nu_\kappa)$ is the term appearing in Lemma~\ref{emin} and $S_{2\varepsilon}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^{n+2}:|x_{n+2}|\le 2\varepsilon\}$ as in \cite{S08}.
nodes.statement_short: The bound gains a term $\sup|P||S_{2\varepsilon}\cap B_1|$.

nodes.name: Normal coordinates
nodes.statement: We remark also that in the proof of this claim, one uses ``rescalings'' of sets in $M\times\mathbb{R}$ and of the measures $\mu_t^k, \mu_t$, which are defined via the exponential map. In particular one makes the identifications \[(B_\rho(x), g)\simeq(B_\rho(\vec 0), \exp^*_x g)\simeq (B_\rho(0), \hat g_{ij}^\phi)\] as Riemannian manifolds, where $(B_\rho(x), \phi)$ are the geodesic normal coordinates that correspond to the identification $(T_pM, g(p))\simeq(R^{n+2}, \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ as Hilbert spaces and $\hat g_{ij}^\phi=g_{ij}^\phi\circ\phi^{-1}$, where $\hat g_{ij}^\phi$ are the components of $g$ in geodesic normal coordinates. These identifications allow us to reduce the proof to the case that $M=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescalings via normal coordinates reduce to $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Invariance
nodes.statement: We remark also that, since $\exp^{-1}$ is an isometry, the minimizing property given in Lemma~\ref{emin} and Claim 2 (both of which are used in the proof of this claim) are preserved under these identifications. For a detailed discussion and proofs of these facts see \cite{Alex}.
nodes.statement_short: The minimizing property and Claim 2 survive the identifications.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Finally, Claim 3 and Claim 4 imply that $\theta(x)=1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}$. Thus, the limit measure $\mu$ does not depend on the subsequence and thus the whole sequence converges $\mu_t^k\to \mu_t$.
nodes.statement_short: $\theta=1$, so the limit is independent of the subsequence.

nodes.name: Claim 1: support of the limit measure
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 1:} $\mathrm{spt} \mu\subset\{u=t\}\times\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Claim 2: density bound for the limit measure
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 2:} For $B_\rho(x)\subset\subset\Omega_0\times\mathbb{R}$ \[\mu(\overline B_\rho(x))\le \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\partial B_\rho(x))+C(K)\mathcal{H}^{n+2}(B_\rho(x)).\]

nodes.name: Claim 3: lower density bound
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 3:} $\theta\ge 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Claim 4: upper density bound
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 4:} $\theta\le 1$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. on $\partial^*E_t$.

nodes.name: $\mu=\mu_t\llcorner\theta$
nodes.statement: \mu=(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(\partial^*E_t\times\mathbb{R}))\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta=\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\theta,

u_k)|^2d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\ &=\liminf_k\int_{\Omega_0	imes I_0}|H^k_t+ P(
u_k)|^2d\mu_t^k<\infty. \end{split} \]
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2$ bound on $H+P$ and Fatou give finite liminf for a.e. $t$.

nodes.name: Subsequence
nodes.statement: Considering such a $t$, we conclude that there exists a subsequence $\{k_i\}_i$ (depending on $t$) such that \begin{equation} \sup_{i\ge 0}\int_{\Omega_0\times I_0}|H_t^{k_i}+P(\nu_{k_i})|^2d\mu_t^{k_i}\le C. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Pick a subsequence with uniformly bounded $\int|H+P|^2$.

nodes.name: $L^2$ bound on $H$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{H+Pki} and the triangle inequality, we obtain that for all $i\in\mathbb{N}$ and any compact subset $W\subset\Omega_0\times I_0$ \begin{equation} \int_{(\Omega_0\times I_0)\cap W}|H_t^{k_i}|^2d\mu_t^{k_i}\le C( \Omega, K, n, W), \end{equation} where we have also used that $|P(\nu_{k_i})|$ is bounded and that, by Remark~\ref{area bound}, the graphs $\widetilde \Sigma_t^{k_i}$ have uniformly bounded area in $W$ so that $\int_{(\Omega_0\times I_0)\cap W}d\mu_t^{k_i}\le C=C(|\Omega|, |\partial\Omega|, \lambda)$, where $\lambda=\max_i\{|\lambda_i|, \lambda_i\text{ eigenvalue of } K\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality and area bounds give a local $L^2$ bound on $H^{k_i}_t$.

nodes.name: Allard compactness
nodes.statement: We have shown thus that $\widetilde\Sigma_t^{k_i}$ have locally uniformly bounded in $L^2$ first variation in $\Omega_0\times I_0$, and since they also have locally uniformly bounded area, we can apply the varifold compactness theorem of Allard \cite{Al}, which yields that, after passing to a further subsequence, $\widetilde\Sigma_t^{k_i}$ converge in the varifold sense to an $(n+1)$-dimensional integral varifold. Since, by Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}, $\mu_t^k\to \mu_t=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(\Sigma_t\times\mathbb{R})$, we obtain that for a.e. $t>0$ \begin{equation} \widetilde\Sigma^{k_i}_t\to \Sigma_t\times I_0=\Sigma_t\times (-1,1)\,\,\,\text{in }\Omega_0\times I_0=\Omega_0\times(-1,1), \end{equation} in the sense of varifolds, where $\Sigma_t\times I_0$ is an $(n+1)$-dimensional rectifiable unit density varifold.
nodes.statement_short: Allard's compactness theorem gives varifold convergence to $\Sigma_t\times I_0$.

nodes.name: Generalized mean curvature of the limit
nodes.statement: The varifold convergence and ~\eqref{Ht2bound} implies that $\Sigma_t\times I_0$ carries a generalized mean curvature vector $\vec H_t$ and $\mu^{k_i}_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu H_t^{k_i}\nu_{k_i}\to\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \vec H_t$ as vector valued Radon measures. By the lower semicontinuity of the first variation and \eqref{Ht2bound}, we have \begin{equation} \int_{\Omega_0\times I_0}|\vec H_t|^2d\mu_t\le \liminf_i\int_{\Omega_0\times I_0}|H^{k_i}_t|^2d\mu^{k_i}_t\le C=C(\Omega, \Omega_0,K,n). \end{equation} Since $\Sigma_t\times I_0$ is a rectifiable unit density varifold, $\vec H_t$ is perpendicular to $\Sigma_t\times I_0$ $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$-a.e. (see \cite[Chapter 5]{B}).
nodes.statement_short: The limit carries a perpendicular generalized mean curvature with $L^2$ bound.

nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity gives (51).

Hence, using \eqref{H+Plimit}, Fatou's lemma, \eqref{24I0} and the uniform area bounds of Remark~\ref{area bound}, we obtain \begin{equation*} \int_0^\infty\int_{\Omega_0\times I_0}|H_t+P(\nu)|d\mu_tdt\le C(\Omega, \Omega_0, K, n). \end{equation*}

nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_t^k=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \widetilde \Sigma_t^k$ and $\mu_t=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^*\widetilde E_t$ (where we use the notation of Definition~ef{U}). Then, for a.e $t\ge 0$ there exists a subsequence $\{k_i\}_i$ (depending on $t$) such that \[\widetilde\Sigma^{k_i}_t	o \Sigma_t	imes (-1,1)\,\,\,	ext{in }\Omega_0	imes(-1,1), \] as varifolds, where $\Sigma_t	imes (-1,1)$ is a rectifiable unit density varifold that carries a generalized mean curvature vector $\vec H_t= H_t

We note that, because of the product structure of the varifold $\Sigma_t	imes (-1,1)$ in Theorem~ef{mainconvii}, for the $n$-dimensional rectifiable unit density varifolds $\Sigma_t$ we have  egin{equation}  egin{split} \int_0^\infty\int_{\Omega}|H_t+P(

nodes.name: Proof that the limit of level sets is a generalized MOTS
nodes.statement:
Estimate \eqref{H+Ptlimi} allows us to pick a sequence of times $t_i\uparrow \infty$ such that  egin{equation} \lim_{i	o\infty}\int_{\Omega}|H_{t_i}+P(
u)|d\mu_{t_i}=0. \end{equation} By the minimizing property, Lemma~ef{eminu} (see also Remark~ef{area bound}), $|\Sigma_{t_i}|$ are uniformly bounded (recall that $\mathcal{H}^n(\Sigma_{t_i}\setminus\partial^*E_{t_i})=0$ by Lemma~ef{bdrystar}) and thus, after passing to a subsequence, $\mu_{t_i}	o \mu_\infty$, where $\mu_\infty$ is a Radon measure in $\Omega$. Furthermore, considering $E_{t_i}$ as finite perimeter sets and using the compactness for such sets, we obtain that, passing to a further subsequence, $E_{t_i}	o E_\infty$ (that is $\chi_{E_{t_i}}	o \chi_{E_\infty}$ with respect to the $L^1(\Omega)$ norm), where $E_\infty$ is a finite perimeter set in $\Omega$. Moreover, since $D\chi_{E_\infty}=(\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u_\infty$ as vector valued measures, where $
u_\infty$ is the measure theoretic outer pointing unit normal to $E_\infty$ (see for example \cite[Section 5.7]{EG92}), we have the convergence $\mu_{t_i}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u	o(\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu
u_\infty$. (The definitions and the theorems used in relation with the finite perimeter sets can be found for example in \cite[Chapters 1 and 3]{Giu}, see also \cite{Alex} for the extensions of these results for finite perimeter sets in a manifold). We claim now that one can argue as in Lemma~ef{mainconvergence} to show that $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^n \hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$. In particular we have the following  egin{Lemma} Assume that $\mu_{t_i}=\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\Sigma_{t_i}	o\mu_\infty$ as Radon measures and $E_{t_i}	o E_\infty$ as finite perimeter sets (where we use the notation of Definition~ef{U}). Then  egin{equation} \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^* E_\infty. \end{equation} \end{Lemma}  egin{proof} The proof is exactly as in Claims 2-4 of the proof of Lemma~ef{mainconvergence}, using now the measures $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ and $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ (instead of $\mu_t$ and $\mu$, see \eqref{mumut}) and therefore we will not repeat it here. We point out that, to fit the notation of this lemma, one has to replace $\Omega_0, \mu_t^k, \widetilde E_t^k$ and $
u_k$ (of Lemma~ef{mainconvergence}) by $\Omega, \mu_{t_i}, E_{t_i}$ and $
u$ respectively and also replace both $\Sigma_t$ and $\partial^*\widetilde E_t$ by $ \partial^* E_\infty$. We also remark that in the proof here we need to use Lemma~ef{eminu} instead of Lemma~ef{emin} (or rather its corollary given in Remark~ef{minimrmk}) and the lower semicontinuity of finite perimeter sets (lower semicontinuity of BV functions) instead of that for Radon measures for the convergence $E_{t_i}	o E_\infty$. \end{proof} We claim now that $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^*E_\infty$ has a generalized mean curvature $\vec H_\infty=H_\infty
u_\infty$ and it furthermore satisfies $H_\infty+P(
u_\infty)=0$, where recall that $
u_\infty$ is the measure theoretic outer pointing unit normal to $E_\infty$. This will then imply that $\partial^*E_\infty$ is a generalized MOTS in the sense of Definition~ef{weakMOTS}. To this aim we will argue as with the convergence in \eqref{varconv} replacing now $\widetilde \Sigma^{k_i}_t$ by $\Sigma_{t_i}$. By the structure theorem for finite perimeter sets (see for example \cite[Section 5.7]{EG92}), we know that for $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. $x\in\partial^*E_\infty$ there exists $B_r(x)\subset M$ so that $E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$ is $C^1$, that is  egin{equation} \partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)=\partial E_\infty\cap B_r(x)	ext{ is a }C^1 	ext{ manifold}. \end{equation} Furthermore, as mentioned before, we have $\|D\chi_{E_\infty}\|=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty$. Note now, that \eqref{H+Ptlimi}, implies that  egin{equation} \sup_{i\ge 0}\int_{\Omega}|H_{t_i}|^2d\mu_{t_i}\le C. \end{equation} \eqref{Htlimibound} shows that $\Sigma_{t_i}$ have uniformly bounded in $L^2$ first variation in $\Omega$, and since they also have uniformly bounded area, we can apply the varifold compactness theorem of Allard \cite{Al}. Therefore, after passing to a subsequence, $\Sigma_{t_i}	o \Sigma_\infty$ in $\Omega$ in the sense of varifolds, where $\Sigma_\infty$ is an integral $n$-dimensional varifold in $\Omega$ which carries a weak mean curvature $\vec H_\infty$ for which the bound \eqref{Htlimibound} still holds. Furthermore, $\vec H_\infty$ is perpendicular to $\Sigma_\infty$ $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. (see \cite[Chapter 5]{B}) and $\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(H_{t_i} 
u)	o \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\vec H_\infty$, where $\mu_\infty$ is the weight measure of $\Sigma_\infty$. We can now relate the varifold limit $\Sigma_\infty$ with $\partial^*E_\infty$ (the limit of finite perimeter sets or currents) by using \cite{W08}. In particular, by \cite[Theorem 1.2]{W08}, $\Sigma_\infty$ and $\partial^*E_\infty$ are compatible, that is $\Sigma_\infty=\underline{\underline{	ext{v}}}(\partial^* E_\infty)+ 2V$, where $V$ is some integral varifold in $\Omega$ and $\underline{\underline{	ext{v}}}(\partial^* E_\infty)$ is the varifold determined by $\partial^*E_\infty$ (see \cite[\S27]{LSgmt}). Using this, \eqref{C1mfld} (that is the structure theorem for sets of finite perimeter) and Lemma~ef{mainconvII}, we conclude that for $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. $x\in\partial^*E_\infty$ there exists $B_r(x)\subset M$ so that $\partial^*E_\infty\cap B_r(x)=\partial E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$ is $C^1$ and furthermore $\Sigma_\infty=\partial E_\infty$ as varifolds in $B_r(x)$ (where in this last equality $\partial E_\infty$ is seen as a unit density varifold, the support of which is a $C^1$ manifold). For the generalized mean curvature of $\Sigma_\infty$ in $B_r(x)$ we then have that $\vec H_\infty=H_\infty
u_\infty$ and $\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(H_{t_i} 
u)	o \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu H_\infty
u_\infty$. Using this, the measure convergence (Lemma~ef{mainconvII}) and the convergence $\mu_{t_i}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u	o(\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu
u_\infty$, we can argue as in \eqref{H+Plimit}, using again the Reshetnyak continuity and the lower semicontinuity, to conclude that \[\int_{\partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)}| H_\infty+ P(
u_\infty)|d\mathcal{H}^n\le \liminf_i\int_{B_r(x)}|H_{t_i}+P(
u)|d\mu_{t_i}.\] Finally, using \eqref{to0} we obtain \[\int_{\partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)}| H_\infty+ P(
u_\infty)|d\mathcal{H}^n=0,\] which implies that $H_\infty(y)+P(
u_\infty(y))=0$ for $\mathcal{H}^n$-a.e. $y\in \partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$. Recalling the definition of a weak solution (Definition ef{weak}) and that for the domain $\Omega_1$ (\eqref{uetou}, see also Lemma ef{bdrystar}), we have therefore shown the following.

nodes.name: Choose times
nodes.statement: Estimate \eqref{H+Ptlimi} allows us to pick a sequence of times $t_i\uparrow \infty$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{i\to\infty}\int_{\Omega}|H_{t_i}+P(\nu)|d\mu_{t_i}=0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Compactness
nodes.statement: By the minimizing property, Lemma~\ref{eminu} (see also Remark~\ref{area bound}), $|\Sigma_{t_i}|$ are uniformly bounded (recall that $\mathcal{H}^n(\Sigma_{t_i}\setminus\partial^*E_{t_i})=0$ by Lemma~\ref{bdrystar}) and thus, after passing to a subsequence, $\mu_{t_i}\to \mu_\infty$, where $\mu_\infty$ is a Radon measure in $\Omega$. Furthermore, considering $E_{t_i}$ as finite perimeter sets and using the compactness for such sets, we obtain that, passing to a further subsequence, $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$ (that is $\chi_{E_{t_i}}\to \chi_{E_\infty}$ with respect to the $L^1(\Omega)$ norm), where $E_\infty$ is a finite perimeter set in $\Omega$.
