nodes.statement:
Moreover, since $D\chi_{E_\infty}=(\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u_\infty$ as vector valued measures, where $
u_\infty$ is the measure theoretic outer pointing unit normal to $E_\infty$ (see for example \cite[Section 5.7]{EG92}), we have the convergence $\mu_{t_i}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u	o(\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu
u_\infty$. (The definitions and the theorems used in relation with the finite perimeter sets can be found for example in \cite[Chapters 1 and 3]{Giu}, see also \cite{Alex} for the extensions of these results for finite perimeter sets in a manifold).
nodes.statement_short: $\mu_{t_i}\llcorner\nu$ converges to $\mathcal H^n\llcorner\partial^*E_\infty$ times $\nu_\infty$.

nodes.name: Density one on the reduced boundary (inner lemma)
nodes.statement: We claim now that one can argue as in Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence} to show that $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^n \hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$. In particular we have the following \begin{Lemma} Assume that $\mu_{t_i}=\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\Sigma_{t_i}\to\mu_\infty$ as Radon measures and $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$ as finite perimeter sets (where we use the notation of Definition~\ref{U}). Then \begin{equation} \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^* E_\infty. \end{equation} \end{Lemma} \begin{proof} The proof is exactly as in Claims 2-4 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}, using now the measures $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ and $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ (instead of $\mu_t$ and $\mu$, see \eqref{mumut}) and therefore we will not repeat it here. We point out that, to fit the notation of this lemma, one has to replace $\Omega_0, \mu_t^k, \widetilde E_t^k$ and $\nu_k$ (of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}) by $\Omega, \mu_{t_i}, E_{t_i}$ and $\nu$ respectively and also replace both $\Sigma_t$ and $\partial^*\widetilde E_t$ by $ \partial^* E_\infty$. We also remark that in the proof here we need to use Lemma~\ref{eminu} instead of Lemma~\ref{emin} (or rather its corollary given in Remark~\ref{minimrmk}) and the lower semicontinuity of finite perimeter sets (lower semicontinuity of BV functions) instead of that for Radon measures for the convergence $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 38 and its proof: $\mu_\infty=\mathcal H^n$ on $\partial^*E_\infty$.

nodes.name: Claim: $H_\infty+P(\nu_\infty)=0$
nodes.statement:
We claim now that $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^*E_\infty$ has a generalized mean curvature $\vec H_\infty=H_\infty
u_\infty$ and it furthermore satisfies $H_\infty+P(
u_\infty)=0$, where recall that $
u_\infty$ is the measure theoretic outer pointing unit normal to $E_\infty$. This will then imply that $\partial^*E_\infty$ is a generalized MOTS in the sense of Definition~ef{weakMOTS}. To this aim we will argue as with the convergence in \eqref{varconv} replacing now $\widetilde \Sigma^{k_i}_t$ by $\Sigma_{t_i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim the reduced boundary has generalized mean curvature with $H_\infty+P(\nu_\infty)=0$.

nodes.name: Consequence
nodes.statement: This will then imply that $\partial^*E_\infty$ is a generalized MOTS in the sense of Definition~\ref{weakMOTS}.
nodes.statement_short: This makes $\partial^*E_\infty$ a generalized MOTS.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: To this aim we will argue as with the convergence in \eqref{varconv} replacing now $\widetilde \Sigma^{k_i}_t$ by $\Sigma_{t_i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Argue as for (49) with $\Sigma_{t_i}$.

nodes.name: Structure theorem
nodes.statement: By the structure theorem for finite perimeter sets (see for example \cite[Section 5.7]{EG92}), we know that for $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. $x\in\partial^*E_\infty$ there exists $B_r(x)\subset M$ so that $E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$ is $C^1$, that is \begin{equation} \partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)=\partial E_\infty\cap B_r(x)\text{ is a }C^1 \text{ manifold}. \end{equation} Furthermore, as mentioned before, we have $\|D\chi_{E_\infty}\|=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: A.e. point of $\partial^*E_\infty$ has a $C^1$ neighbourhood.

nodes.name: $L^2$ mean curvature bound
nodes.statement: Note now, that \eqref{H+Ptlimi}, implies that \begin{equation} \sup_{i\ge 0}\int_{\Omega}|H_{t_i}|^2d\mu_{t_i}\le C. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Uniform $L^2$ bound on $H_{t_i}$.

nodes.name: Allard compactness
nodes.statement: \eqref{Htlimibound} shows that $\Sigma_{t_i}$ have uniformly bounded in $L^2$ first variation in $\Omega$, and since they also have uniformly bounded area, we can apply the varifold compactness theorem of Allard \cite{Al}. Therefore, after passing to a subsequence, $\Sigma_{t_i}\to \Sigma_\infty$ in $\Omega$ in the sense of varifolds, where $\Sigma_\infty$ is an integral $n$-dimensional varifold in $\Omega$ which carries a weak mean curvature $\vec H_\infty$ for which the bound \eqref{Htlimibound} still holds. Furthermore, $\vec H_\infty$ is perpendicular to $\Sigma_\infty$ $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. (see \cite[Chapter 5]{B}) and $\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(H_{t_i} \nu)\to \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\vec H_\infty$, where $\mu_\infty$ is the weight measure of $\Sigma_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Varifold limit $\Sigma_\infty$ with generalized mean curvature.

nodes.name: Compatibility with the reduced boundary
nodes.statement: We can now relate the varifold limit $\Sigma_\infty$ with $\partial^*E_\infty$ (the limit of finite perimeter sets or currents) by using \cite{W08}. In particular, by \cite[Theorem 1.2]{W08}, $\Sigma_\infty$ and $\partial^*E_\infty$ are compatible, that is $\Sigma_\infty=\underline{\underline{\text{v}}}(\partial^* E_\infty)+ 2V$, where $V$ is some integral varifold in $\Omega$ and $\underline{\underline{\text{v}}}(\partial^* E_\infty)$ is the varifold determined by $\partial^*E_\infty$ (see \cite[\S27]{LSgmt}). Using this, \eqref{C1mfld} (that is the structure theorem for sets of finite perimeter) and Lemma~\ref{mainconvII}, we conclude that for $\mathcal{H}^{n}$-a.e. $x\in\partial^*E_\infty$ there exists $B_r(x)\subset M$ so that $\partial^*E_\infty\cap B_r(x)=\partial E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$ is $C^1$ and furthermore $\Sigma_\infty=\partial E_\infty$ as varifolds in $B_r(x)$ (where in this last equality $\partial E_\infty$ is seen as a unit density varifold, the support of which is a $C^1$ manifold).
nodes.statement_short: By White [W08], $\Sigma_\infty=v(\partial^*E_\infty)+2V$, so locally $\Sigma_\infty=\partial E_\infty$.

nodes.name: $H_\infty+P=0$
nodes.statement:
For the generalized mean curvature of $\Sigma_\infty$ in $B_r(x)$ we then have that $\vec H_\infty=H_\infty
u_\infty$ and $\mu_t\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu(H_{t_i} 
u)	o \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu H_\infty
u_\infty$. Using this, the measure convergence (Lemma~ef{mainconvII}) and the convergence $\mu_{t_i}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu 
u	o(\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^* E_\infty)\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu
u_\infty$, we can argue as in \eqref{H+Plimit}, using again the Reshetnyak continuity and the lower semicontinuity, to conclude that \[\int_{\partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)}| H_\infty+ P(
u_\infty)|d\mathcal{H}^n\le \liminf_i\int_{B_r(x)}|H_{t_i}+P(
u)|d\mu_{t_i}.\] Finally, using \eqref{to0} we obtain \[\int_{\partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)}| H_\infty+ P(
u_\infty)|d\mathcal{H}^n=0,\] which implies that $H_\infty(y)+P(
u_\infty(y))=0$ for $\mathcal{H}^n$-a.e. $y\in \partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reshetnyak continuity, lower semicontinuity and (53) give $H_\infty+P(\nu_\infty)=0$ a.e.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Recalling the definition of a weak solution (Definition \ref{weak}) and that for the domain $\Omega_1$ (\eqref{uetou}, see also Lemma \ref{bdrystar}), we have therefore shown the following.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $\partial^*(\Omega\setminus\Omega_1)$ is a generalized MOTS.

nodes.name: Density one of the limit measure on $\partial^*E_\infty$
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mu_{t_i}=\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\Sigma_{t_i}\to\mu_\infty$ as Radon measures and $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$ as finite perimeter sets (where we use the notation of Definition~\ref{U}). Then \begin{equation} \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^* E_\infty. \end{equation}
assumptions: $\mu_{t_i}=\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\Sigma_{t_i}\to\mu_\infty$ as Radon measures and $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$ as finite perimeter sets
nodes.label: mainconvII

nodes.name: $\mu_\infty\llcorner\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal H^n\llcorner\partial^*E_\infty$
nodes.statement: \mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty=\mathcal{H}^{n}\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu \partial^* E_\infty.
nodes.label: muinfty

nodes.name: Proof of density one
nodes.statement: The proof is exactly as in Claims 2-4 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}, using now the measures $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ and $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ (instead of $\mu_t$ and $\mu$, see \eqref{mumut}) and therefore we will not repeat it here. We point out that, to fit the notation of this lemma, one has to replace $\Omega_0, \mu_t^k, \widetilde E_t^k$ and $\nu_k$ (of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}) by $\Omega, \mu_{t_i}, E_{t_i}$ and $\nu$ respectively and also replace both $\Sigma_t$ and $\partial^*\widetilde E_t$ by $ \partial^* E_\infty$. We also remark that in the proof here we need to use Lemma~\ref{eminu} instead of Lemma~\ref{emin} (or rather its corollary given in Remark~\ref{minimrmk}) and the lower semicontinuity of finite perimeter sets (lower semicontinuity of BV functions) instead of that for Radon measures for the convergence $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat Claims 2-4 of the measure convergence proof with the minimization property of Lemma 34.

nodes.name: Same as Claims 2-4
nodes.statement: The proof is exactly as in Claims 2-4 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}, using now the measures $\mathcal{H}^n\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ and $\mu_\infty\hbox{ {\vrule height .25cm}{\leaders\hrule\hskip.2cm}}\hskip5.0\mu\partial^*E_\infty$ (instead of $\mu_t$ and $\mu$, see \eqref{mumut}) and therefore we will not repeat it here.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat Claims 2-4 of Lemma 36 with the new measures.

nodes.name: Notation changes
nodes.statement: We point out that, to fit the notation of this lemma, one has to replace $\Omega_0, \mu_t^k, \widetilde E_t^k$ and $\nu_k$ (of Lemma~\ref{mainconvergence}) by $\Omega, \mu_{t_i}, E_{t_i}$ and $\nu$ respectively and also replace both $\Sigma_t$ and $\partial^*\widetilde E_t$ by $ \partial^* E_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the notation of this lemma.

nodes.name: Changed ingredients
nodes.statement: We also remark that in the proof here we need to use Lemma~\ref{eminu} instead of Lemma~\ref{emin} (or rather its corollary given in Remark~\ref{minimrmk}) and the lower semicontinuity of finite perimeter sets (lower semicontinuity of BV functions) instead of that for Radon measures for the convergence $E_{t_i}\to E_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 34 and BV lower semicontinuity instead.

nodes.name: $C^1$ structure of the reduced boundary
nodes.statement: \partial^* E_\infty\cap B_r(x)=\partial E_\infty\cap B_r(x)\text{ is a }C^1 \text{ manifold}.
nodes.label: C1mfld

nodes.name: Uniform $L^2$ bound on $H_{t_i}$
nodes.statement: \sup_{i\ge 0}\int_{\Omega}|H_{t_i}|^2d\mu_{t_i}\le C.
nodes.label: Htlimibound

nodes.name: Weak solutions converge to a generalized MOTS
nodes.statement: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$ (as in Definition~\ref{weak}). Then $\partial^*(\Omega\setminus\Omega_1)$ is a generalized MOTS, as in Definition~\ref{weakMOTS}.
assumptions: Let $u\in C^{0,1}(\Omega_1)$ be a weak solution of $(**)$ (as in Definition~\ref{weak}).
conclusions: Then $\partial^*(\Omega\setminus\Omega_1)$ is a generalized MOTS, as in Definition~\ref{weakMOTS}.
nodes.label: MOTSconv

nodes.name: The limit is a classical MOTS ($V=0$)
nodes.statement: We believe that $V=0$ and $\partial^*E_\infty=\partial E_\infty$ is actually a MOTS in the classical sense and therefore, as it lies outside the outermost MOTS, it is indeed the outermost MOTS.

nodes.name: Two-sided minimization would pass to the limit
nodes.statement:
In Lemma ef{eminu} we have showed that the level sets $\partial^*E_t$ satisfy a one-sided minimizing property, namely that of minimizing area plus {\it bulk energy P}. This property is inherited from the level sets $\{U_\varepsilon=t\}$ (Lemma ef{emin}). The level sets $\{U_\varepsilon=t\}$ not only minimize ``area $+\int P$'' on the outside, but they also minimize (not only one-sided) ``area $+\int \left(P- rac{1}{|\overline
abla U_\varepsilon|}ight)$'' (Remark ef{minimrmk}). The latter minimizing property would pass to the limit if we have that $|\overline
abla U_\varepsilon|^{-1}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}	o|\overline
abla U|^{-1}d\mathcal{H}^{n+1}$ as radon measures.
nodes.statement_short: The one-sided minimization of level sets is inherited from $U_\varepsilon$; a two-sided version would pass to the limit if $|\overline\nabla U_\varepsilon|^{-1}d\mathcal H$ converges.

nodes.name: Convergence of $|\overline\nabla U_\varepsilon|^{-1}$ measures
nodes.statement: This is indeed true in the case of mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$ as proved in \cite{MS} and we believe that it also true in our case.

nodes.name: Two-sided minimization would give a classical MOTS limit
nodes.statement: Now, if this convergence is true, and thus the level sets $\{u=t\}$ minimize ``area $+\int \left(P-\frac{1}{|\nabla u|}\right)$'', we can use the $L^1$-finiteness of $|\nabla u|^{-1}$ (Lemma \ref{normalintest}) to conclude that as $t\to \infty$ the limit minimizes ``area$+\int P$'' and therefore is a MOTS, with the regularity of the limit coming from the fact that it is a $C$-minimizing current as defined in Section \ref{eexistencesection}.
assumptions: if this convergence is true
conclusions: the limit minimizes ``area$+\int P$'' and therefore is a MOTS

nodes.name: Singular set of null mean curvature flow has small dimension
nodes.statement: In particular we would like to have the following: There exists a singular set $S\subset \mathrm{graph} u$ of parabolic Hausdorff dimension at most $n-1$ outside of which the sets $\{u=t\}$ are a smooth level set flow.

nodes.name: Minimization-based weak solutions and uniqueness
nodes.statement: Finally, we would like to remark that if the level $\{u=t\}$ minimize ``area $+\int \left(P-\frac{1}{|\nabla u|}\right)$'' then we can define a weak solution of $(*)$ using this minimization property, as was done in \cite{MS} for the mean curvature flow (see also \cite{HI01, KM13} for the inverse mean curvature flow and the inverse null mean curvature flow). In \cite{MS}, this definition was used to show that the level set flow is unique and it is not hard to check that the methods from \cite{MS} can be applied to our case to show uniqueness.
